Pattern Zoo — state pre-screen

15 mechanisms, each at state OFF and state ON. The poses are snapped by the engine's own rule — the outline saved in the map is the ON pose, and OFF is that outline minus the marker delta — so these are where the geometry sits, not a guess.

What to look for: does OFF look shut and ON look open, and is that the way round you want? The curtains were backwards twice.

Do not judge these by eye. Each card carries the measured difference between the two states, read back out of the snapped maps: headroom, plan area, and how far the payload sprites actually travel. All 19 mechanisms change measurably, none disagrees with its own declared travel, and three pairs are identical on purpose — those rotors turn whole circles and finish where they began. The pictures are here to tell you which exhibit you are looking at.

tile 142

used on two-sided walls in the campaign despite carrying the mask colour. Sits in the 140s run with 146/147, which are the curtain fabrics -- if it is family, the law needs a two-sided exception for cloth.

Ask: family or accident?

tile 2464

the same breach, far from the 140s and from any cloth. If this one is an accident and 142 is not, the exception is about the 140s family and not about the law.

Ask: family or accident?

Snapped poses, not the game running: nothing here says anything about speed, sound or interruption. A floor mechanism (the casket) shows in neither frame — its lid is beyond the bay's own wall, so no camera in the aisle reaches it; that one has to be walked.
